To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ADR and/or DAU, in combination with Ca(2+) antagonists or PK(C) inhibitors, inhibit the promoting component of mouse skin carcinogenesis by interfering with early biochemical effects of TPA.

ADR and/or DAU, alone, are ineffective in inhibiting the promotion of skin tumours induced by TPA; however, when ADR and/or ADR are used in conjunction with either VRP or PC, the tumour-promoting activity of TPA is inhibited.
the anti-cancer drugs adriamycin (ADR), daunomycin (DAN), and doxorubicin (DOX) alone do not inhibit the promotion of mouse skin papillomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the development of a new approach to the development
the use of Ca2+ antagonistic and PKC inhibitory agents to overcome the drug resistance of cancer cells and to improve the effectiveness of anti-cancer drugs.
the development of a strategy to overcome the resistance to the antitumor effects of ADR or its analogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ADR and/or DAU in combination with Ca(2+)-antagonists and/or PKC inhibitors may have a potential in the treatment of human skin cancers, but that further studies are necessary to establish the efficacy of these combinations in the prevention and/or treatment of human skin cancer.

Ca2+ antagonistic agents and PKC inhibitors may be useful in the therapy of skin carcinogenesis and that anthracycline antitumor antibiotics may be effective in the therapy of human cancer when combined with Ca2+ channel antagonists or PK inhibitors.

the anthracyclines ADR and DAUN are effective inhibitors of tumor promotion only when they are administered simultaneously with Ca2+ channel blockers (e.g. Verapamil) and protein kinase C inhibitors (e.g. Palmitoylcarnatine).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anthracyclines are effective inhibitors of the promoting component of chemical carcinogenesis only when applied in combination with agents that circumvent the drug resistance of the tumor cells.
Ca2+ antagonism or PKC inhibition can circumvent drug resistance and enhance the effectiveness of ADR and DAUs against tumor promotion.
the antitumor effects of ADR and DAUs are revealed only when they are applied in the presence of Ca2+ antagonistic or PKC inhibitory compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of anthracyclines with Ca2+ antagonist or PKC inhibitors may be useful for the prevention of tumor promotion in the skin.
ADR and/or DAU in combination with Ca(2+)-antagonists and/or PKC-inhibitors may be useful in the treatment of human skin cancer.
ADR and/or DAU in combination with VRP or PC may be effective against the promoting phase of skin carcinogenesis.
